contracts.description: The work-layer operations contract: propose (idempotent intake of task proposals carrying spec linkage), report (enumeration of spec-linked tasks with contract statuses), and the op-sequence fixture exchange that proves them.

exclusions: Claims, assignment, scheduling, prioritization semantics, and notification are the work layer's own business and out of scope.
Cross-person claim federation is out of scope (removed deliberately in design v1; do not reintroduce).
How status changes happen natively (UI, CLI, API of the underlying system) is out of scope; only the mapping into the contract vocabulary is normative.
Storage, sync, and identity models of the work layer are out of scope.
goals: Define the MUST-minimal contract between felag-core's audit verb and any work layer, so task systems are swappable and a thin shim over an existing tracker can conform without reimplementation.
Make spec-linked work units recognizable across different people's work layers via specItemRef as the cross-layer identity.
Keep felag-core free of work state: this contract is the only coupling, and it is one-directional (audit proposes; the work layer owns everything after).
name: felag-tasks

body: A conforming work layer holds tasks that MAY carry spec linkage: a specItemRef of the form 'spec:<specName>/<itemId>' and optionally a criterionId. Linkage is the cross-layer identity: two work layers projecting the same (specItemRef, criterionId) hold the same unit of work, whatever else they disagree about. taskRef is an opaque implementation-specific string; it carries no semantics beyond identity within one work layer. For fixture exchange, taskRefs are normalized by order of first appearance to '$1', '$2', ... before comparison, so fixtures are mechanical across implementations. Work-layer binding is personal workstation configuration, never committed project state.
title: Model: tasks as projections of spec items

body: The propose operation accepts a TaskProposal {specItemRef, criterionId?, title, description?, priority?, attribution, at} and returns a ProposalResult {accepted, created, taskRef, errors}. Required fields: specItemRef, title, attribution, at; a proposal missing one is rejected with E_MISSING_FIELD and accepted=false. Idempotency is the load-bearing rule: proposals are keyed on (specItemRef, criterionId), where absent criterionId is a distinct key value; re-proposing an existing key MUST NOT create a duplicate — the result carries created=false and the existing taskRef. Distinct criterionIds under the same specItemRef are distinct tasks. attribution is a free-form attribution string with no semantics.
title: propose — idempotent intake of task proposals

gherkin:
Given an empty conforming work layer
When a valid TaskProposal with specItemRef and title is proposed
Then the result is accepted with created true and a taskRef
And report lists exactly one entry for that linkage with status open

Given a work layer holding a task for (specItemRef, criterionId)
When the same (specItemRef, criterionId) is proposed again
Then the result is accepted with created false and the existing taskRef
And report still lists exactly one entry for that linkage

Given a work layer holding a task for a specItemRef with criterionId A
When the same specItemRef is proposed with criterionId B
Then a second task is created
And report lists two entries under that specItemRef

Given a conforming work layer
When a TaskProposal missing specItemRef is proposed
Then the result is not accepted and errors contains E_MISSING_FIELD
And report lists no entry for it

body: The report operation returns {entries: [{taskRef, specItemRef, criterionId?, status}]} listing every task that carries spec linkage, sorted ascending by (specItemRef, criterionId, taskRef) with absent criterionId sorting before any present value. status MUST be one of the contract vocabulary: open | in_progress | done | cancelled — every native state of the underlying system maps to exactly one contract status; the mapping is the shim's one real job. A task created by propose MUST first report as open. This enumeration is what felag-core's audit reads to compute coverage and to honor proposal idempotency across runs.
title: report — linkage enumeration for coverage

gherkin:
Given a work layer holding several spec-linked tasks
When report is requested
Then entries are sorted ascending by specItemRef, criterionId, taskRef
And every status is one of open, in_progress, done, cancelled

body: A work layer SHOULD accept a transition operation {taskRef, to} where to is a contract status, returning {ok}. Agents normally act in the native layer (that is the point of shims); transition exists so that fully headless flows can close the loop through the contract alone. Implementations that refuse transition still conform to the MUST surface.
title: transition — optional status movement through the contract

gherkin:
Given a work layer holding an open task
When transition moves it to done through the contract
Then the result is ok
And report shows the task with status done

body: A conforming shim over an existing tracker requires mapping only: no storage of its own beyond, at most, the (specItemRef, criterionId) -> native-id index needed for idempotency, and even that SHOULD live in the underlying system where it can (labels, custom fields, description markers). The contract never requires felag-core to be present: a work layer conforms in isolation, exercised purely through op-sequence fixtures.
title: Seams

item: A conforming shim over an existing tracker performs mapping only, holding no task storage of its own beyond an idempotency index, which itself lives in the underlying system where possible.
Work-layer binding is personal workstation configuration and is never committed as project state; collaborators on one spec may run different conforming work layers.
